title: Throw off the cloak: the call to warn
translation: O you wrapped in your cloak, arise and warn! Magnify your Lord, purify your garments, and keep away from defilement.
body: **Nöldeke–Schwally** linked the “cloaked one” to soothsayers who prophesied wrapped in mantles. **Uri Rubin** finds no such reading in tafsir; the oldest glosses likely saw the cloak as **withdrawal from the mission**, which “Arise!” ends. Jeremiah hears the same: “gird up… arise”. Luther, citing Jeremiah’s “hammer”, calls such warning **the law’s thunderbolt**.
question: Is the cloak a sign of fear and withdrawal, a soothsayer’s mantle, or a badge of prophethood?
reading: Uri Rubin, The Eye of the Beholder (1995)
